title: Windows CC build fails with compiler/linker out-of-memory errors under high parallelism
signature: Windows Release build runs out of memory - compiler fatal error C1060 (out of heap space) and linker fatal error LNK1102 (out of memory) under high parallelism|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: Build_And_Run_Collect_Mode
failed_jobs.symptom: Ninja build aborted mid-way: cl.exe fatal error C1060 (compiler out of heap space), c1xx fatal error C1356 (unable to find mspdbcore.dll), and multiple link.exe fatal error LNK1102 (out of memory) for benchmark_app.exe, model_creation_sample.exe, hello_query_device.exe.

failed_jobs.name: ci/gha_overall_status_windows_cc
failed_jobs.symptom: Reports overall failure because the upstream build job failed.

key_errors: C:\BuildTools\VC\Tools\MSVC\14.42.34433\include\xmemory(1509): fatal error C1060: compiler is out of heap space
c1xx: fatal error C1356: unable to find mspdbcore.dll
LINK : fatal error LNK1102: out of memory
root_cause: The Windows Conditional Compilation (Release) build runs with CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=31 (high ninja job parallelism) on a runner with finite RAM. Each parallel MSVC cl.exe/link.exe process for template functional test translation units (e.g. op_reference/*.cpp) and sample executables consumes substantial heap, and once the Release build reaches the tests/functional and samples/link stages the aggregate working set exceeds available memory, causing the compiler front-end (c1xx) to run out of heap space (C1060), fail to load mspdbcore.dll (C1356, itself a symptom of memory exhaustion), and the linker to report LNK1102 out of memory on several executables. This is the same recurring infrastructure/runner-resource pattern recorded 10 times previously (first seen 2026-11-03), not a regression introduced by the triggering commit/PR.
reproduction_steps: N/A (cannot reliably reproduce without the same constrained Windows runner memory/parallelism combination). Locally: build the Release configuration with Ninja Multi-Config and CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL set high (e.g. 31) on a machine with limited RAM relative to core count; compiling src/plugins/template/tests/functional/op_reference/*.cpp in parallel alongside linking benchmark_app/model_creation_sample/hello_query_device reproduces the heap/linker OOM.
recommended_actions: Lower CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL for the Windows Conditional Compilation Release job (or split it into fewer concurrent ninja jobs) to reduce peak memory usage.
Consider building template functional tests and the sample executables in separate ninja invocations/stages rather than all at CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=31 simultaneously.
Evaluate moving this job to a runner SKU with more RAM, or add a /Zc or linker memory-saving flag (e.g. avoid /LARGEADDRESSAWARE duplication seen twice in the link command) where applicable.
Track CVS ticket for infra team to raise/tune build concurrency limits on Windows CC runners given this is the 11th occurrence.
prevention_strategies: Cap ninja/MSBuild parallelism proportionally to available runner RAM (rule of thumb ~1.5-2 GB per parallel MSVC job for this codebase) rather than using core count alone; add a CI pre-check or retry-with-reduced-parallelism fallback when C1060/LNK1102 are detected.
historical_context: Recorded 10 prior occurrences of this exact signature (pattern 80cfa127185fbf3e, first_seen 2026-11-03T07:07:04Z, last_seen 2026-11-18T11:29:31Z) across many unrelated commits, confirming this is a persistent Windows runner resource-constraint issue rather than code introduced by this PR.
